name: Corporate prospecting gifting service
one_liner: Put together personalised gifts that B2B sales teams send to prospects, to say thanks after a signed deal and to clients at the holidays.
customer: B2B sales teams and companies, especially in tech, that do outbound prospecting
offer: Gifts tailored to each recipient, sourced from vendors such as Etsy makers, packed and shipped through the client's own shipping platforms when they have them
how_it_makes_money: A margin on each gift, priced to fit the client's budget. Revenue also comes from repeat campaigns and holiday orders.
evidence: Stay-at-home mum made $357k last year working 20 hours a week (GHU8YdA4kxo)
Grew organically with no marketing spend (GHU8YdA4kxo)
Started for under $1,000; corporate gifting called a $250B industry (GHU8YdA4kxo)
Niche is prospecting for tech companies in Dallas (GHU8YdA4kxo)
risks: Relies on relationships, and her client base is local
Handling physical products and inventory
Demand peaks around the holidays
Margins shrink if clients find the suppliers themselves (one client had already found the mugs on Etsy)

name: Vibe-coded websites for local business owners
one_liner: Build websites for small business owners quickly with AI coding tools and sell them through direct outreach.
offer: Websites built with AI or no-code tools, plus ongoing care
how_it_makes_money: Build fees per project. The transcript does not give the price split or say whether there are retainers.
startup_cost: low (laptop, AI tool subscriptions such as Lovable)
time_to_first_revenue: days to weeks (built in a weekend, first customer targeted within a day)
evidence: $180k in the first 6 weeks; first project brought in $200–300k (J7ZNaOeXCAA)
John Cheney made $2.5M in a year building websites for business owners with AI (J7ZNaOeXCAA)
'There are 33 million business owners' in the US, so 10% of people you know are potential customers (GiGCLwVRoCk)
risks: Very low barrier to entry, so prices are likely to fall
Finding customers is the hard part, and the transcript is vague on how he did it
The headline numbers are likely outliers

name: Niche pain-point micro-SaaS
one_liner: Build a small software tool that fixes one specific workflow problem in a niche you already know.
customer: Practitioners in a niche, such as bloggers, SEOs or developers
offer: Subscription software, for example an internal-linking tool or a social posting app for developers
startup_cost: low (MVP built with AI coding tools)
time_to_first_revenue: months (it was 'crickets for the first month or two'; over $5k/mo within the first year)
evidence: Link Whisper made well over $5k/mo in its first year and is now a 7-figure business (GVSiAvjADBk)
A dev-focused social posting app built by two people who had been laid off now earns MRR above their previous salaries (IywUW2RjXis)
Customers arriving because 'ChatGPT sent me' or Claude recommended them; Google Ads only started after $10k MRR (IywUW2RjXis)
risks: Slow start with no audience
Crowded categories
Needs real knowledge of the niche's pain

name: Generalist-style niche community and newsletter
one_liner: Build a paid community around an underserved identity group, with a newsletter, membership, job board and events.
customer: Professionals who identify with the niche (in the example, career generalists) and employers who post jobs
offer: Newsletter, paid membership, job board listings and a summer school
how_it_makes_money: Membership fees, job board fees, event tickets and sponsorship
evidence: Generalist World makes $30k/month and nearly $600k over 4 years (ICTRNFIdZvc)
Run by a solo founder with a small team from a Scottish island of 191 people (ICTRNFIdZvc)
risks: Needs a long audience build
Depends on the founder's personal brand and writing
The transcript does not break down revenue by stream

name: Global remote talent placement
one_liner: Place vetted offshore talent who use AI tools with small businesses, on annual contracts.
how_it_makes_money: Annual contracts priced as a markup on talent cost (one contract was worth $30k a year)
startup_cost: low (Lovable, Wi-Fi and a recruiting platform stated)
evidence: '$100k in 100 days' after a 1 March launch (GiGCLwVRoCk)
Won a $30,000/year contract by walking into the prospect's office in person (GiGCLwVRoCk)
'Global talent plus AI is the absolute sauce' (GiGCLwVRoCk)
risks: The model details are vague in the transcript (evidence weak to medium)
Quality control and churn
The biggest win came from in-person selling

name: Own-brand physical product on Shopify
one_liner: Launch a niche physical product through your own Shopify store and use Amazon and other marketplaces as extra channels.
customer: Online consumers in a niche (in the example, buyers of thin pillows)
how_it_makes_money: Product margin. The business can also be sold later (exited for $425k).
evidence: Pillow business made over $10k/mo in its first 12 months and sold for $425k (GVSiAvjADBk)
risks: Inventory and cash tied up in stock
Ad costs
The case is from a few years ago, and the speaker himself would rely less on Amazon now

name: Garage epoxy and concrete coating
one_liner: Apply premium epoxy flake coatings to garage floors for wealthy homeowners.
offer: Garage and concrete floor coating installation
how_it_makes_money: Priced per job, at $3–4k profit per job day. A $200 referral fee produced a $30k job.
startup_cost: low to medium (under $1,000 stated, plus tools)
time_to_first_revenue: weeks ($60k in the first full month)
evidence: Started in March, then $60k in April and $69k the next month, booked a month ahead (HcR7Wqgi4lU)
risks: Physical work done in person
Does not fit a founder who is time-constrained and wants async work
The owner already had 5 years in trades
